a: Name of the API. Must be less than or equal to 128 characters in length.
API key selection expression. Valid values: `$context.authorizer.usageIdentifierKey`, `$request.header.x-api-key`. Defaults to `$request.header.x-api-key`. Applicable for WebSocket APIs.
OpenAPI specification that defines the set of routes and integrations to create as part of the HTTP APIs. Supported only for HTTP APIs.
Part of _quick create_. Specifies any credentials required for the integration. Applicable for HTTP APIs.
Description of the API. Must be less than or equal to 1024 characters in length.
Whether clients can invoke the API by using the default `execute-api` endpoint. By default, clients can invoke the API with the default `{api_id}.execute-api.{region}.amazonaws.com endpoint`.
Whether warnings should return an error while API Gateway is creating or updating the resource using an OpenAPI specification. Defaults to `false`. Applicable for HTTP APIs.

IP address types that can invoke the API. Valid values: `ipv4`, `dualstack`. Use `ipv4` to allow only IPv4 addresses to invoke your API, or use `dualstack` to allow both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses to invoke your API.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Part of _quick create_. Specifies any route key. Applicable for HTTP APIs.
Route selection expression for the API. Defaults to `$request.method $request.path`.
Map of tags to assign to the API. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
Map of tags assigned to the resource, including those inherited from the provider `default_tags` configuration block.
Part of _quick create_. Quick create produces an API with an integration, a default catch-all route, and a default stage which is configured to automatically deploy changes.
Version identifier for the API. Must be between 1 and 64 characters in length.
Whether credentials are included in the CORS request.
Number of seconds that the browser should cache preflight request results.
Domain name. Use the `aws_apigatewayv2_domain_name` resource to configure a domain name.
API stage. Use the `aws_apigatewayv2_stage` resource to configure an API stage.
API mapping key. Refer to REST API, HTTP API or WebSocket API.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Authorizer type. Valid values: `JWT`, `REQUEST`. Specify `REQUEST` for a Lambda function using incoming request parameters. For HTTP APIs, specify `JWT` to use JSON Web Tokens.
Name of the authorizer. Must be between 1 and 128 characters in length.
Required credentials as an IAM role for API Gateway to invoke the authorizer. Supported only for `REQUEST` authorizers.
Format of the payload sent to an HTTP API Lambda authorizer. Required for HTTP API Lambda authorizers. Valid values: `1.0`, `2.0`.

Time to live (TTL) for cached authorizer results, in seconds. If it equals 0, authorization caching is disabled. If it is greater than 0, API Gateway caches authorizer responses. The maximum value is 3600, or 1 hour.

Authorizer's URI. For `REQUEST` authorizers this must be a well-formed Lambda function URI, such as the `invoke_arn` attribute of the `aws_lambda_function` resource. Supported only for `REQUEST` authorizers.
Whether a Lambda authorizer returns a response in a simple format. If enabled, the Lambda authorizer can return a boolean value instead of an IAM policy. Supported only for HTTP APIs.
Identity sources for which authorization is requested. For `REQUEST` authorizers the value is a list of one or more mapping expressions of the specified request parameters.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
List of the intended recipients of the JWT. A valid JWT must provide an aud that matches at least one entry in this list.
Base domain of the identity provider that issues JSON Web Tokens, such as the `endpoint` attribute of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource.
Description for the deployment resource. Must be less than or equal to 1024 characters in length.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Map of arbitrary keys and values that, when changed, will trigger a redeployment. To force a redeployment without changing these keys/values, use the `terraform taint` command.
Domain name. Must be between 1 and 512 characters in length.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Mode to route traffic for the domain name. Valid values: `API_MAPPING_ONLY`, `ROUTING_RULE_ONLY`, `ROUTING_RULE_THEN_API_MAPPING`.
Map of tags to assign to the domain name. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
Map of tags assigned to the resource, including those inherited from the provider `default_tags` configuration block.

ARN of an AWS-managed certificate that will be used by the endpoint for the domain name. AWS Certificate Manager is the only supported source. Use the `aws_acm_certificate` resource to configure an ACM certificate.
TLS version of the security policy for the domain name. Valid values: `TLS_1_2`.
IP address types that can invoke the domain name. Valid values: `ipv4`, `dualstack`.

ARN of the AWS-issued certificate used to validate custom domain ownership (when `certificate_arn` is issued via an ACM Private CA or `mutual_tls_authentication` is configured with an ACM-imported certificate.)

Amazon S3 URL that specifies the truststore for mutual TLS authentication, for example, `s3://bucket-name/key-name`. The truststore can contain certificates from public or private certificate authorities.
Version of the S3 object that contains the truststore. To specify a version, you must have versioning enabled for the S3 bucket.

Integration type of an integration. Valid values: `AWS` (supported only for WebSocket APIs), `AWS_PROXY`, `HTTP` (supported only for WebSocket APIs), `HTTP_PROXY`, `MOCK` (supported only for WebSocket APIs).
ID of the VPC link for a private integration. Supported only for HTTP APIs. Must be between 1 and 1024 characters in length.
Type of the network connection to the integration endpoint. Valid values: `INTERNET`, `VPC_LINK`. Default is `INTERNET`.
How to handle response payload content type conversions. Valid values: `CONVERT_TO_BINARY`, `CONVERT_TO_TEXT`. Supported only for WebSocket APIs.
Credentials required for the integration, if any.
Integration's HTTP method. Must be specified if `integration_type` is not `MOCK`.
AWS service action to invoke. Supported only for HTTP APIs when `integration_type` is `AWS_PROXY`. See the AWS service integration reference documentation for supported values.
URI of the Lambda function for a Lambda proxy integration, when `integration_type` is `AWS_PROXY`. For an `HTTP` integration, specify a fully-qualified URL.
Pass-through behavior for incoming requests based on the Content-Type header in the request, and the available mapping templates specified as the `request_templates` attribute.
Format of the payload sent to an integration. Valid values: `1.0`, `2.0`. Default is `1.0`.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
For WebSocket APIs, a key-value map specifying request parameters that are passed from the method request to the backend.
Map of Velocity templates that are applied on the request payload based on the value of the Content-Type header sent by the client. Supported only for WebSocket APIs.
Template selection expression for the integration.

Custom timeout between 50 and 29,000 milliseconds for WebSocket APIs and between 50 and 30,000 milliseconds for HTTP APIs. The default timeout is 29 seconds for WebSocket APIs and 30 seconds for HTTP APIs.
Key-value map. The key of this map identifies the location of the request parameter to change, and how to change it. The corresponding value specifies the new data for the parameter.
HTTP status code in the range 200-599.

If you specify a server name, API Gateway uses it to verify the hostname on the integration's certificate. The server name is also included in the TLS handshake to support Server Name Indication (SNI) or virtual hosting.
How to handle response payload content type conversions. Valid values: `CONVERT_TO_BINARY`, `CONVERT_TO_TEXT`.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Map of Velocity templates that are applied on the request payload based on the value of the Content-Type header sent by the client.
Template selection expression for the integration response.
Content-type for the model, for example, `application/json`. Must be between 1 and 256 characters in length.
Name of the model. Must be alphanumeric. Must be between 1 and 128 characters in length.
Schema for the model. This should be a JSON schema draft 4 model. Must be less than or equal to 32768 characters in length.
Description of the model. Must be between 1 and 128 characters in length.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Route key for the route. For HTTP APIs, the route key can be either `$default`, or a combination of an HTTP method and resource path, for example, `GET /pets`.
Whether an API key is required for the route. Defaults to `false`. Supported only for WebSocket APIs.
Authorization scopes supported by this route. The scopes are used with a JWT authorizer to authorize the method invocation.
Authorization type for the route. For WebSocket APIs, valid values are `NONE` for open access, `AWS_IAM` for using AWS IAM permissions, and `CUSTOM` for using a Lambda authorizer.
Identifier of the `aws_apigatewayv2_authorizer` resource to be associated with this route.
Model selection expression for the route. Supported only for WebSocket APIs.
Operation name for the route. Must be between 1 and 64 characters in length.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Request models for the route. Supported only for WebSocket APIs.
Route response selection expression for the route. Supported only for WebSocket APIs.
Target for the route, of the form `integrations/`*`IntegrationID`*, where *`IntegrationID`* is the identifier of an `aws_apigatewayv2_integration` resource.
Request parameter key. This is a request data mapping parameter.
Model selection expression for the route response.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Response models for the route response.
Domain name. Must be between 1 and 512 characters in length.
Order of rule evaluation. Priority is evaluated from the lowest value to the highest value. Rules can't have the same priority. Value must be between 1 and 1,000,000.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
API identifier of the target API.
Whether to strip the base path when forwarding the request to the target API.
List of strings of the case sensitive base path to be matched.
Case insensitive header name to be matched. The header name must be less than 40 characters and the only allowed characters are a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and the following special characters: *?-!#$%&'.^_`|~.

Name of the stage. Must be between 1 and 128 characters in length.
